calls.action: Run `python3 .pilot/pilot.py resolve review 9` (no --auto, no --resume); the pick is claim-fresh for ticket #70, so go to the claim (doctor is skipped, it already reported ok).

Claim the ticket: `python3 .pilot/pilot.py claim review 70 --mode fresh` (no --merge, no --auto). Assignee and status:in-review are set and re-read. On lost-race or any other refusal, stop and report.
Push the claim's event/activity to the dashboard with ArtifactData (ToolSearch to load it if deferred). The dashboard URL is set.
Ask the human once whether anything specific should be checked in the PR. Keep the answer to pass to the reviewer in step 5.

Read ticket #70 and its own type:tech label. Fetch the PR's changed files (get_files) and run `pilot.py workflow show --ticket 70 --path <changed files>` to get the reviewer set. The lean workflow means pilot-techlead alone. Check get_reviews for a prior submitted review (none expected on a first round). No --with or --only.
If the project has a CI workflow covering the affected area, check it is green on the PR head commit. Red or pending counts as an automatic `change` point. Otherwise this is a no-op.

Make one Agent call for pilot-techlead (no --multi). Pass pilot-link-review-consensus.md, pilot-link-existing-analysis.md and pilot-task-review-spec-conformance.md in full. Also pass the PR diff and description, the ticket spec, the knowledge/wiki/architecture link docs in full, the PR's wiki/ and architecture/ changes, the wiki entries for ticket #70 (wiki index --ticket 70, wiki show <id>), and the human's specific points from the earlier question.
Aggregate the tech lead's verdict into exactly one outcome: approved, change only, decision only, or change plus decision. (Step 5a is skipped because there is only one instance.)

Checkpoint the outcome: create a pending PR review (`mcp__github__pull_request_review_write` method create, commitID pinned to the head, no event). The body carries the full outcome, including the tech lead's Checked against list.

If the outcome carries needs-human, skip the pause and go straight to step 9. Otherwise (all-approve or pure-change), show the outcome. The human decides: confirm, drop or add points, or flip approve and change. Update the pending review to match, quoting dropped points as dropped.

Submit the pending review with submit_pending, using the event that matches the outcome (APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES or COMMENT). Apply the label with `pilot.py set 70 --status approved|changes-requested --unassign`, adding `--add needs-human` where the outcome has a decision point. A decision-only outcome keeps status:in-review and uses `--add needs-human` alone. If GitHub rejects the event because the identity is the PR author, retry submit_pending on the same review with COMMENT.

Only if the outcome carried needs-human (decision-only or mixed): engage the live human on the block. If their answer changes the outcome, create and submit one more review with the matching event and label, plus the why/what comment and a second resolution comment, removing needs-human. If the block is not cleared, leave it standing.
Report the outcome: the verdict, the label set, and that the PR was not merged (no --merge was passed, so step 12 is skipped and a human merges). Step 11 is only a limit of at most two reviews.
